questions.question:
P, Q, R, S and T are sitting on a bench facing towards north but not necessarily in the same order. P is immediate neighbour of Q, S is immediate neighbour of T. P is not sitting with R who sits on the right end of the bench. P sits to the right of S and T. S sits to the right of T.

In which position P is sitting?
questions.solution:
Given: P, Q, R, S and T are sitting on a bench facing towards north but not necessarily in the same order. 

1) P is not sitting with R who sits on the right end of the bench.

2) P is immediate neighbour of Q.

3) P sits to the right of S and T.

4) S is immediate neighbour of T and S sits to the right of T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e7635a13e08805e6a0d3b746ac20b62ec97fb27493597936a4da057c8dfd4944.png] 

So, P is sitting at the '**Third from left**' place.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question:

441 ∶ 9261 ∶∶ 169 ∶ ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: 1st number **×** **(****√**1st number) = 2nd number.

Now,

For 441 ∶ 9261

→ 441 × (√441)

→ 441 × 21 = 9261.

Similarly, for **169 ∶ ?**

**→ 169 × (√169)**

**→ 169 × 13 = 2197.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. Eg 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

(6, 4, 48)

(8, 5, 80)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number **×** 2nd number) × 2 = 3rd number.

Now,

For (6, 4, 48)

→ (6 × 4) × 2

→ 24 × 2 = 48.

For (8, 5, 80)

→ (8 × 5) × 2

→ 40 × 2 = 80.

Similarly, for **Option 1: (3, 7, 42)**

**→ (3 × 7) × 2**

**→ 21 × 2 = 42.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No plate is Mug.

Some Mugs are Tables.

**Conclusions:**

I. All plates being tables is a possibility.

II. Some tables are not mugs.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follow.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

No plate is Mug.

Some Mugs are Tables.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b03e8dd5fb07c5725112d6cc6fafe1ce0493741ecc9e2c1857e184a53cca21f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All plates being tables is a possibility - True (Because, No definite relation given between plates and tables, so All plates being tables can be possible).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9244689d2397c63a30b04e341ca4f32167c080a9ac519a152f1c52a4f3a7a216.png] 

II. Some tables are not mugs - False (Because, Some tables are mugs, but no information given to the remaining part, so only possibility can be true here).

So, Only conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question: Five boys Aman, Baman, Chaman, Daman and Farhan have different ages. Farhan is elder than only Aman and Baman. Daman is younger than only Chaman. Aman is not the youngest. How many boys are elder than Aman?
questions.solution:
Given: Five boys Aman, Baman, Chaman, Daman and Farhan have different ages.

1) Daman is younger than only Chaman.

Chaman > Daman > __ > __ > __

2) Farhan is elder than only Aman and Baman.

3) Aman is not the youngest.

Chaman > Daman > Farhan > Aman > Baman

So, total '**3**' boys are elder than Aman.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

questions.question:
A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Four of them are sitting at each of the corners, while the other four are sitting at the exact centre of each of the sides.

E who sits at the centre of a side, sits to the fourth left of the G. Only one person sits between G and F. B is immediate neighbour of E. Only three people sit between B and A. A is not a neighbour of D. H sits to the immediate left of C. C sits second to the right of E.

Who sits fourth to the right of D?
questions.solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Four of them are sitting at each of the corners, while the other four are sitting at the exact centre of each of the sides.

1) E who sits at the centre of a side, sits to the fourth left of the G. 

2) Only one person sits between G and F. 

3) B is immediate neighbour of E. 

4) C sits second to the right of E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70e8ddc19929c20ed2a628a95240db07eca2854e93348272fedc661b8ac6728f.png] 

5) Only three people sit between B and A.

6) A is not a neighbour of D.

7) H sits to the immediate left of C. 

And, D will sit on the remaining place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c7e4bc7cdc828c299b8c2ed5382d34250ed2613622f2a0977210267f2724457.png] 

So, 'H' sits fourth to the right of D.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All carrots are vegetables.

Some vegetables are snacks.

**Conclusions:**

I. All vegetables are carrots.

II. All carrots are snacks.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All carrots are vegetables.

Some vegetables are snacks.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b6e7e34657e3dcb069fa863e569b3e901e92bbf5524e83ab3aa175935ff4c83.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All vegetables are carrots - False (Because, All carrots are vegetables gives some vegetables are carrots but All vegetables are carrots can be possible only).

II. All carrots are snacks - False (Because, No definite relation given between carrots and snacks).

So, Neither conclusion I nor II follow. 

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
By interchanging the given two signs which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and -

I. 4 × 6 + 7 - 3 ÷ 1 = 21

II. 6 × 9 + 7 - 8 ÷ 2 = 51
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation I. 4 × 6 + 7 - 3 ÷ 1 = 21

Now, if '+ and -' are interchanged, then:

⇒ 4 × 6 - 7 + __**3 ÷ 1**__ = 21

⇒ __**4 × 6**__ - 7 + 3 = 21

⇒ __**24**__ - 7 __**+ 3**__ = 21

 __27 - 7__ = 21

**⇒ 20 ≠ 21.**

Given equation II. 6 × 9 + 7 - 8 ÷ 2 = 51

Now, if '+ and -' are interchanged, then:

⇒ 6 × 9 - 7 + __**8 ÷ 2**__ = 51

⇒ __**6 × 9**__ - 7 + 4 = 51

⇒ __**54**__ - 7 __**+ 4**__ = 51

⇒ __58 - 7__ = 51.

Here, **Option 1 is not correct**.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
